title: France Antarctique
capsule: France Antarctique was a French colonial venture in Guanabara Bay (present-day Rio de Janeiro), established on 1 November 1555 when Vice-Admiral Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon led two ships and some 200 soldiers and colonists to construct Fort Coligny on a small island, naming the mainland settlement Henriville in honor of King Henri II. The colony attracted 300 additional settlers in 1557, including 14 Calvinist missionaries sent by John Calvin, whose presence triggered a fierce dispute over the Eucharist that ended with the Calvinists' expulsion. Portuguese Governor-General Mem de Sá destroyed Fort Coligny in 1560; his nephew Estácio de Sá founded Rio de Janeiro in 1565 and delivered the final defeat on 20 January 1567, extinguishing the French presence on the Brazilian coast.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The colony's location on the island of Serigipe in Guanabara Bay is well-attested; the coastal zone it claimed to control (Rio to Cabo Frio) is described in contemporary accounts but was never systematically surveyed.
